title: Flooded-home re-entry gate
summary: Use a strict go-or-no-go check for official clearance, electricity, gas, structure, water, mould, animals, and contamination before entering.
content: Action sequence: Confirm authorities allow return and inspect from outside for leaning walls, roof movement, foundation damage, fallen wires, gas odour, fire, and standing water. Ensure electricity and gas hazards are controlled by qualified services before touching wet systems. Enter with another adult, daylight, communication, a time limit, and a clear exit; photograph before moving items. Separate salvage, hazardous waste, food, medicines, porous contaminated items, documents, and valuables into marked zones. Safety boundary: Do not enter a restricted or structurally uncertain building. Do not use matches, switches, appliances, or engines where gas or electrical damage may exist.

title: Clean-zone and dirty-zone setup after contamination
summary: Prevent mud, sewage, chemicals, mould, or animal waste from being carried into sleeping, food, and medication areas.
content: Action sequence: Place the dirty zone at the entry closest to the contaminated work and the clean zone upwind or away from drainage and dust. Set a one-way sequence for removing tools, boots, outer clothing, waste, handwashing, and entering the clean area. Use separate labelled tools and containers; never return a dirty item to clean storage without appropriate cleaning. Keep children, animals, food, drinking water, medicines, and bedding outside the work zone. Safety boundary: Do not mix cleaning chemicals or create fumes in a poorly ventilated space. Do not eat, drink, smoke, or handle medicines inside the dirty zone.

title: Mould growth stop rule after water damage
summary: Define when a small drying task must stop and become a professional remediation problem because exposure, hidden spread, or structural damage is too great.
content: Action sequence: Identify the water source and stop it safely before drying or removing material. Document affected rooms, dates, odour, visible growth, porous materials, ventilation, and symptoms among occupants. Keep vulnerable people away and use methods that limit dust and spores rather than spreading them through the home. Stop and seek qualified help for large areas, hidden wall or ventilation contamination, sewage or chemical water, structural damage, or significant health symptoms. Safety boundary: Do not dry-brush, sand, or use a fan that blows contamination into clean rooms. Do not occupy a visibly contaminated or strongly odorous sleeping area merely because the surface feels dry.

title: Disaster photograph and evidence workflow
summary: Create useful evidence for safety, insurance, landlord, municipal support, and repair without entering danger or exposing private information.
content: Action sequence: Photograph the outside and every room from safe fixed positions before moving items. Include wide views, close details, labels, serial numbers, water lines, cracks, utility damage, and a date reference. Keep a written index linking each image group to location, item, observed condition, and action taken. Back up the files, preserve originals, and share copies only with authorized recipients. Safety boundary: Do not cross barriers, enter unstable areas, or touch live utilities to obtain a better photograph. Do not post identity documents, exact addresses, medical records, keys, or security details publicly.

title: Return-to-home essentials inspection
summary: Decide whether a home is usable by checking structure, exits, water, sanitation, power, food, sleeping space, communications, and access needs.
content: Action sequence: Confirm official re-entry permission and a safe structure, entrance, exit, stairs, roof, and balcony. Verify drinking-water status, toilet and wastewater function, safe power, ventilation, and absence of gas or carbon-monoxide hazards. Inspect food, medicines, bedding, child and animal areas, communication, and the ability to call for help. If any critical function is unsafe, choose temporary accommodation and write exactly what must be repaired or verified before return. Safety boundary: Do not treat electricity, water, gas, sanitation, or structural safety as acceptable merely because some rooms look normal. Do not return a vulnerable person before their specific access, medicine, temperature, and support needs are working.
